Lessons.Title: Exponential and Logarithmic Models
ExplanationParagraphs: Exponential growth/decay f(t)=A0e^(kt) has initial A0>0 and rate k, positive for growth, negative for decay.
Half-life T>0 leads to A(t)=A0(1/2)^(t/T). Doubling time for growth k>0 is ln2/k.
Newton's cooling is T(t)=Ts+(T0−Ts)e^(−kt); the sign of T0−Ts determines approach direction.
Logistic growth L/(1+ae^(−kt)), L>0, a>0, k>0, approaches carrying capacity L; time to double depends on starting point.
Fit a model to observed data by using constant ratios, constant differences, or logarithmic shape. Do not extrapolate beyond meaningful physical conditions.
With b>0, b!=1, b^t=e^((ln b)t); y=ln(x²) is defined for x≠0, while 2lnx requires x>0.
Orders of magnitude compare multiplicative factors of 10. Plot powers of ten by their common logarithms.
Independent Cool-down: (a) 50g with half-life4h at12h, (b) find a logistic carrying capacity, (c) compare domains of ln(x²) and2lnx.
Independent Try It 1: Give model for100g, half-life4h.
Independent Try It 2: Time until25% remains if half-life8 years.
Independent Try It 3: Doubling time for P(t)=20e^(0.1t).
Independent Try It 4: Cool liquid50° in room70°; after1h it is60°. When will it be65°?
Independent Try It 5: Estimate P(2) for P=200/(1+3e^(−.8t)).
Independent Try It 6: Classify data x=1,2,3 y=4,8,16.
Independent Try It 7: Rewrite f(x)=4(0.7)^x in e-base form.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exponential models
KeyConcepts.Rule: Positive k growth; negative k decay.

KeyConcepts.Title: Half-life and doubling
KeyConcepts.Definition: T_half=ln2/|k| for exponential decay; T_double=ln2/k for growth.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use correct units and positive time.

KeyConcepts.Title: Model fitting
KeyConcepts.Definition: Choose linear, exponential, logarithmic or logistic according to observed change and context.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Verify domain and recognize extrapolation limits.
KeyConcepts.Example: log₂(x) fits doubling x with additive y increments.

SummaryPoints: Growth and decay rates determine time behavior.
Select models from data and interpret log scale.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat logistic doubling time as constant.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Solve for target population using the specific logistic equation.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat an indefinite exponential forecast as guaranteed.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Finite resources and changing physical conditions invalidate long-term extrapolation.
